{
  "summary": "Replaces raw integer time constants and arithmetic with `std::chrono` duration types and literals across consensus parameters, validation, mempool, networking, RPC, and the GUI. Where existing subsystem interfaces still require integer seconds, durations are converted at the call site with explicit division (e.g. `duration / 1s`). Characterization tests are also added to verify that proof-of-work timing and the assumevalid horizon values remain unchanged.",
  "problem": "Multiple subsystems represent time intervals as raw integers (typically seconds), leaving units implicit in code and allowing differing time units or unrelated numeric values to be mixed without compiler protection.",
  "evidence": [
    "Author's PR description: \"Several fixed-duration calculations use raw integer time counts, leaving their units implicit and allowing unrelated integer values to be mixed.\"",
    "Commit messages note that tests in `pow_tests.cpp`, `chain_tests.cpp`, and `feature_assumevalid.py` were added or updated specifically to pin the exact values before migrating to chrono types."
  ],
  "dependencies": {

result.summary: Replaces raw integer time constants and arithmetic with `std::chrono` duration types and literals across consensus parameters, validation, mempool, networking, RPC, and the GUI. result.card: Converts various duration calculations and constants across GUI, RPC, net, mempool, and validation code from raw integers to typed std::chrono durations. This makes duration units explicit in code and prevents accidental unit mismatches, accompanied by characterization tests ensuring zero numeric divergence in PoW spacing and assumevalid calculations. It is an internal refactoring without bug fixes or user-visible behavioral changes.
